, while ginseng cell cultures are not yet ready for full-scale commercial production, they have great promise as an efficient and environmentally benign alternative to field cultivation.

ginseng cell suspension culture has the potential to produce ginseng biomass, ginseng sponins and ginseng polysaccharides in a large scale, but the productivity of gingseng biomass, saponins and polysaccharides are still far below that of the field cultivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ginseng cell cultures have been successfully used to produce ginseng biomass, ginsenoside, and polysaccharides.

ginseng cell cultures can produce ginseng biomass, saponin and other bioactive components at a level comparable to those obtained from field-grown ginseng plants, but the productivity of ginesol, the major ginseng volatile component, is still very low.
the productivity of gineseng biomass and useful components can be enhanced by optimizing the culture medium and culture conditions, and by genetic manipulation of the cultured cells.
